critical_code_review_comments: server.py:493 — POST /awaits/{id}/snooze DB-sets attentionState=NORMAL, but compute_attention() in the response overrides to OVERDUE when expectedAt<today. This is correct system behavior (attentionState is derived from expectedAt) but the review-request spec wording 'sets attentionState NORMAL' can be misread: for overdue items the API response still returns OVERDUE. Pytest picks a non-overdue item to assert NORMAL. Consider a code comment on compute_attention noting the intentional derivation.

server.py:610 — recap 'slipped' is computed as open items with expectedAt in last 7 days OR whose expectedAt was pushed this week. Works well; be aware very old overdue items whose expected date was set >7 days ago will not appear in 'slipped' — this matched the visible UI (Insurance shows as overdue in recap-owes but is 'slipped' only when pushed).
